wasser: Boil water for at least one minute (three minutes at elevations above 6,500 feet or 2,000 meters) to kill harmful bacteria, viruses and parasites. Let the water cool, then store it in clean, covered containers. Store at least one gallon of water per person per day for at least three days.
blutung: Apply direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth or sterile gauze. Do not remove the cloth if it soaks through; add more layers on top. If bleeding from an arm or leg is life-threatening and does not stop with pressure, apply a tourniquet two to three inches above the wound, never over a joint, and note the time it was applied.
unterkuehlung: Hypothermia is a medical emergency that occurs when the body loses heat faster than it can produce it, causing a dangerously low body temperature, below 95°F (35°C). Signs include shivering, slurred speech, drowsiness and confusion. Move the person to a warm place, remove wet clothing, and warm the center of the body first: the chest, neck, head and groin.
lebensmittel: Never leave perishable food out for more than two hours, or one hour if the temperature is above 90°F. Cook poultry to an internal temperature of 165°F (74°C). A refrigerator will keep food safely cold for about four hours during a power outage if the door is kept closed.
kohlenmonoxid: Carbon monoxide is an odorless, colorless gas that can kill within minutes. Never run a generator, grill or camp stove inside your home, garage or tent. Place generators at least 20 feet from windows and doors.
paracetamol: Paracetamol is a common painkiller used to treat aches and pains. It can also be used to reduce a high temperature. Adults can take one or two 500mg tablets up to four times in 24 hours, leaving at least 4 hours between doses. Do not take more than 8 tablets in 24 hours.
verbrennung: For minor burns, cool the burn under cool (not cold) running water for 20 minutes. Do not apply ice, butter or toothpaste. Cover the burn loosely with a clean non-stick dressing or cling film. Seek emergency help for burns larger than the person's palm, or burns on the face, hands, feet or genitals.
austrocknung: Signs of dehydration include dark yellow urine, dry mouth, headache and dizziness. In severe cases, a person may have a rapid heartbeat and sunken eyes. Give small, frequent sips of an oral rehydration solution: one liter of clean water with six level teaspoons of sugar and half a level teaspoon of salt.
funk: In an emergency, tune a battery-powered or hand-crank radio to the NOAA Weather Radio frequencies between 162.400 and 162.550 MHz to receive alerts. Keep spare batteries in your emergency kit.
verstauchung: Follow the RICE method for a sprain: rest, ice, compression and elevation. Apply an ice pack wrapped in a towel for 15 to 20 minutes every two to three hours for the first 48 hours.
